page.layout: One block of verse in the centre of the page, italic lines with a centred small-capital heading inside it; below it, at the right, a catchword-like word "Viro" (signature-like). No margin notes, no running head, no page number.

main_text.p:
Paucissimusque vix celebratam libris.
Hic picta tantum Veritas acquiritur,
Quam radiolis a Sole per nubeculas
Adspersa Ratio adumbrat ideis suis.
Hinc Solis umbram vivido sine lumine
Tantum gerit, nec frena vel virgam tenet
Imbellis, animos nec coercens, nec regens.

Hac vero quanto dignior nubes procul
Transvecta, cuboque insidens immobilis
In monte lato apparet ERUDITIO
SOLIDA, rudes quae sola mentes perpolit
Pertinne cujus possidens Solis jubar
Angusta nil sinit latere dextera,
Longaque noctis dira solvit vincula:
Sinistra vero frena virgamque afferens
Animosa corda temperat feliciter,
Pedesque dirigit Salutis in viam.

Ad hanc, procul post se relictis omnibus,
Juvenis Viator, nudus a praejudiciis,
Solus licet, nec obrutus libris, gradu
Votisque seriis anhelat, impiger.
Nec fallet illum spes: profanos nam quidem
A monte murus arcet; at fideliter
Pulsantibus tandem patebit janua;
Qui sic refecti fructibus montis sacri
Laeta deinceps verticem ascendant via,
Ferantque digna pro labore pramia.

page.notes: The verse is printed in italic with some words in small capitals (ERUDITIO, SOLIDA). The word "Viro" at lower right is set in italic and may be a catchword or signature; it is transcribed as printed. Some letters are faint or broken by specks, notably "Pertinne" and "Pulsantibus", which may be misprints or damage; the reading "Pertinne" is doubtful. Long s has been rendered as s throughout.
